---
title: "check-serial-comma.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that fails when a pull request adds a list of three or more items
with no comma before the final "and" or "or".
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-11-03; Morrison-Lab/psw grammar chapter) is to write
"mean, median, and mode", so the reader never has to guess
whether the last two items form a pair.

The check joins each paragraph before matching,
so a list split across lines by semantic line breaks is still found.
It reduces math, code, links, and citations to placeholders,
and skips an introductory phrase followed by a pair ("However, x and y"),
"such as" and "for example" phrases, code fences, HTML comments,
YAML front matter, and table rows.
A line carrying `<!-- check-serial-comma: allow -->` is exempt.

An untouched line is never reflagged.
With no base ref the check skips instead of scanning the whole tree;
`whole-tree` measures a corpus.
The match is a heuristic, not a parser, so the allow marker is the escape hatch.

## Usage

Copy
[`examples/check-serial-comma.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-serial-comma.yml)
to `.github/workflows/` in your repository.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | `*.qmd *.md` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check |
| `paths-ignore` | empty | Comma- or newline-separated git pathspecs to skip, such as `_extensions/**,latex-macros/**` |
| `fail` | `true` | Fail the workflow on a finding instead of warning |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Scan every file, not only a PR's additions |
| `runs-on` | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label; self-hosted only for a private repository |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version to set up |
